the model says the meaning changed: The worker now opens a job-failed debugging case after three consecutive failures even when the judge was simply unreachable (dispatch step), but SR-245 says an unreachable judge only makes records wait with one line, and a debugging case is expected only for an out-of-schema retry that cannot be settled (EX-11).; filed as a question for the owner, to ask with the question tool: The requirement still matches what you asked for. When no judge can be reached, iaso should say so once per session window, keep only the unanswered records waiting, and let everything else go on. Opening a debugging case is described in one situation only: the judge gave a malformed answer, the records were retried, and the job still couldn't be settled (EX-11).

The code used to make one exception. When a job failed three times in a row only because there was no model to ask, it opened no debugging case, because that is a setup problem outside iaso and a bigger retry budget can't fix it. The change removed that exception. Now a judge that stays unreachable opens a "job failed three times in a row" debugging case like any other failure. That adds a second signal on top of the single waiting line, and it treats a missing key or a service outage as iaso's own bug.

What's unclear: none of the requirement's examples says outright that an unreachable judge must never open a debugging case, so I can't say for certain that an example is broken. The prompt that probably made the change was "continue your investigation and try to understand what's going on", so the exception may have been removed on purpose to make these failures easier to see while debugging. Or it may have been removed by accident. I can't tell which, so this needs your decision.; the card is not offered until it is complete, it lacks: what option 1 ("Put the exception back: an unreachable judge only makes records wait with one line and never opens a debugging case") does and leaves undone; what option 2 ("Keep the change and reword the requirement: after three unreachable-judge failures in a row, iaso also opens one debugging case") does and leaves undone; what option 3 ("Keep a debugging case only for failures that aren't about reaching the judge (a malformed answer, a diff too large), and keep plain unreachability out") does and leaves undone; why the recommended option is recommended (iaso stale card SR-245#14 --consequences "..." --why "...")
